Renders any filter-driven set of tiddlers as a slide deck with reveal.js-style 2D navigation (left/right between sections, up/down between slides within a section), link-driven deep-dive with a breadcrumb that pops you back, and a pluggable layout system. ## Key features - **Filter-parameterized** — pass any filter that yields slide-tiddler titles in order. Not coupled to any specific content model. - **2D navigation** — `←/→` walks horizontally between sections; `↑/↓` walks vertically between slides within the current section. - **Deep-dive breadcrumb** — clicking a wikitext link inside a slide pushes the current location and renders the linked tiddler as an ad-hoc slide. The breadcrumb above the slide shows where you came from; click any segment to pop back. - **Pluggable layouts** — `mm.slide-layout` on each slide selects a layout template under `$:/plugins/rimir/present/layouts/`. Ships with `default`, `title`, `two-column`, `quote`, `image`, `full`. Add your own by creating a layout tiddler. - **Notes + help** — `N` toggles presenter notes (configurable field); `?` shows the keyboard reference. - **Engine-agnostic** — companion plugins (such as `rimir/mindmap`) supply the filter via a wikitext op; this plugin just plays. ## Prerequisites - TiddlyWiki 5.3.0+ - Optional: `rimir/theme` for shared `rr-` style hooks - Optional: `rimir/doc-template` for the branded documentation tab ## Quick start ``` <$present slides="[tag[Slides]]" section-field="mm.slide-of" layout-field="mm.slide-layout" caption-field="caption" notes-field="mm.slide-notes" title="My deck" /> ``` Wrap in `$reveal` to gate the overlay on a state tiddler if you want a button to "play" the deck. ## License MIT. Pipeline # ''Filter resolution'' — at `render()` time, the widget evaluates `slides=` against the widget context to get an ordered list of slide tiddler titles. # ''Grid construction'' — for each slide, the widget reads the `section-field` and groups consecutive slides with the same value into one //section//. Sections are the horizontal axis; slides within a section are the vertical axis. Slides without a section-field value get their own solo bucket (so two unrelated tiddlers don't accidentally bucket together). # ''Chrome render'' — a fixed-position fullscreen overlay, structured as `top-bar | stage | bottom-HUD`. The stage is where slide content lives; the top bar carries the deck title, breadcrumb, and action buttons; the HUD carries position counter and current-slide caption. # ''Current-slide render'' — the widget resolves the slide's `layout-field` (default `mm.slide-layout`) to a tiddler under `$:/plugins/rimir/present/layouts/`; if missing, falls back to `default`. It builds a one-shot wikitext widget tree `<$tiddler tiddler=<>><$transclude $tiddler=<>/>` which gives the layout template access to the slide's fields via `<>` and `{{!!field}}`. !! State model The widget keeps //navigation state// in instance variables (not in state tiddlers): `this.section`, `this.slide`, `this.stack` (array of stack entries), and `this.deepTiddler` (current ad-hoc slide title or null). State tiddlers are only used to drive //open/close// from outside, via `<$reveal>` wrapping the widget — that way, opening a presentation is a one-line state-tiddler write from anywhere in the wiki. Closing fires `on-close-actions` (typical: clear the open-state tiddler). The parent `$reveal` sees the clear and calls our widget's `removeChildDomNodes`, which tears down the keydown listener and the overlay DOM. !! Navigation stack Each stack entry is one of: * `{ kind: "grid", section: i, slide: j }` — a position in the deck grid (the deck root, before any deep-dive). * `{ kind: "deep", tiddler: "..." }` — an off-path tiddler reached by clicking a link. Diving into a tiddler pushes a snapshot of the //current// location onto the stack and sets `deepTiddler`. Popping (via Esc, the Home button, or a breadcrumb segment) walks back. The breadcrumb above the slide stage renders the stack as clickable chips; the leftmost chip (`⌂`) is always present and pops everything. A deep-dive view always renders with the `default` layout — using the slide's own layout would be wrong (you've dived //off// the deck path; the layout was meant for a different slide). !! Link interception Clicks inside the stage bubble up to a single delegated handler. The handler walks the event target up until it hits either an `` element or a `.tc-tiddlylink` (TW's `<$link>` produces these). The target title is read in order from: # `data-tiddler-title` (set by TW's `<$link>` widget) # `data-tw-target-title` (alternative; rarer) # `href` attribute (plain anchors) Internal links that resolve to a tiddler trigger a deep-dive. External links (no tiddler resolves) fall through to the browser default — open in a new tab as normal. !! Performance The widget renders //only the current slide// — neighbours are not pre-rendered. Each navigation tears down the previous slide widget tree and builds the new one. For decks with under a few hundred slides this is more than fast enough and avoids issues with embedded heavy widgets (mindmaps, graphs) being kept warm for slides the user never reaches. Example 1 — minimal flat deck Plain tagged slides; no grouping; arrows walk linearly. ``` <$button> <$action-setfield $tiddler="$:/state/my-deck/open" text="yes"/> Play deck <$reveal state="$:/state/my-deck/open" text="yes" type="match"> <$present slides="[tag[Slides]sort[order]]" section-field="—" title="My deck" on-close-actions="<$action-setfield $tiddler='$:/state/my-deck/open' text=''/>" /> ``` Setting `section-field="—"` (a field nobody will have) makes every slide its own section — arrow keys then behave linearly, no vertical-stack confusion. !! Example 2 — grouped deck Each top-level section gets its own column of slides; vertical arrows walk within a section. Author slides with fields: * `tags: Slides` * `section: intro` (or `body`, `wrap-up`, …) * `caption: …` * body text = wikitext Then play with: ``` <$present slides="[tag[Slides]sort[order]]" section-field="section" caption-field="caption" title="Q2 review" /> ``` !! Example 3 — playing a mindmap presentation If you're using `rimir/mindmap` v0.3.0+, presentations are first-class. Set `mm.presentation` on a view tiddler, then click ''▶ Play'' in the preview-pane's Presentation tab (header bar or next to the modebar dropdown) — or press ''Shift+F2'' when focused in the canvas. The page-template tiddler that handles the activation is `$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/templates/present-overlay`. It reads the active presentation from `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/present-target` and wires the deck via the `mm-presentation-slides` filter operator. !! Example 4 — authoring a custom layout Add a tiddler `$:/plugins/rimir/present/layouts/bullets`: ``` \procedure render-bullets()

{{!!caption}}

<$list filter="[has[mm.slide-bullets]]" variable="_">
    <$list filter="[get[mm.slide-bullets]split[\n]!is[blank]]" variable="line">
  • <$wikify name="r" text=<>><>
\end render-bullets <$transclude $variable="render-bullets"/> ``` Then on a slide tiddler set `mm.slide-layout=bullets` and put your bullet lines in `mm.slide-bullets` (one per line). Why two plugins instead of bundling the player into mindmap? Because "play a sequence of tiddlers" is broader than "play mindmap slides". A separate player keeps the data shape (filters yielding tiddlers) decoupled from the data source (mindmap, a tagged set, a generated list, a Trello-style board, anything else). Mindmap supplies the filter operator that flattens a presentation into slide titles; the player doesn't know or care where those titles came from. !!! How does the deep-dive work — am I just opening tiddlers? Yes — clicking a wikitext link inside a slide //navigates inside the overlay//. The widget intercepts the click, pushes the current location onto an internal stack, and re-renders the stage with the linked tiddler as a one-shot slide (using the `default` layout). The breadcrumb at the top shows the depth; click any segment to pop back, or use Esc which pops one level at a time. Once the stack is empty, Esc closes the overlay. !!! Can the player remember my position across reloads? No — navigation state is in-memory only by design. A presentation is a single live session; mid-session reloads aren't a use-case we support. If you need bookmarkable slide positions, write a thin wrapper that mirrors the state into a `$:/state/` tiddler. !!! How big can a deck be? Practically unlimited — only the current slide renders. Decks of hundreds of slides are fine. Decks of thousands of slides will be fine to play but slow to //compute the grid// (the widget evaluates the filter once and walks every result to read its section-field). !!! Why does Space behave differently from →? `→` always moves to the next section (jumping past any remaining vertical slides). `Space` is //linear//: it goes down within the current section first, only jumping right when the bottom of the section is reached. That mirrors reveal.js and matches the "walk the entire deck" mental model. !!! Why does Esc not close immediately when I've dived deep? So you can dive into a referenced tiddler during a Q&A, then Esc back to where you were — the same use-case as a back button in a browser. If you want one-press exit no matter what, pop everything first with the `⌂` button and Esc once. !!! Are external links followed normally? Yes — only links that resolve to a tiddler in the wiki trigger a deep-dive. Anything else (URLs, mailto, anchors that don't resolve) falls through to the browser's default handling. "},"$:/plugins/rimir/present/doc/overview":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/present/doc/overview","created":"20260513000000000","modified":"20260513000000000","rdt.hub-category":"visualization","rdt.hub-category-name":"Visualization & Layout","rdt.hub-order":"25","rdt.order":"1","rdt.plugin-key":"present","rdt.plugin-name":"present","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Fullscreen slide player with 2D nav and deep-dive breadcrumb","rdt.section":"Overview","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! What it does `rimir/present` ships a single widget — `$present` — that takes a //filter// yielding ordered tiddler titles and plays them as a fullscreen slide deck. The deck is engine-agnostic: any plugin or hand-authored wikitext that can produce an ordered list of slide tiddlers can drive a presentation. The widget is designed for two use-cases: * ''Sequenced playback'' — walk a deck linearly with arrow keys or space. * ''Discussion-driven dive-in'' — during a talk, click any link in a slide to "dive in" to that tiddler, with a breadcrumb that pops you back to where you came from. !! Why it exists The mindmap plugin (`rimir/mindmap`) ships a //slides as tiddlers// model — each slide is a real tiddler with `caption` / `mm.slide-layout` / `mm.slide-notes` / body — and named-presentation tiddlers (`mm.slides-order`) that group nodes' slides into a playlist. Until v0.3.0, no player existed: slides could be authored and previewed but not played. The natural shape was //two plugins//, not one — the player is a generic slide stage, the mindmap supplies the data. This plugin is that player. !! Features * ''Filter-parameterized slide source'' — `slides=""`. No coupling to any data model. * ''reveal.js-style 2D navigation'' — `←/→` between //sections// (top-level groups), `↑/↓` between //slides// within a section. Sections are derived from a configurable group-field on each slide tiddler. * ''Deep-dive breadcrumb'' — clicking a wikitext link inside a slide pushes the current location onto a navigation stack and renders the linked tiddler as an ad-hoc slide. The breadcrumb at the top shows where you came from; clicking any crumb pops back. `Esc` pops one level; pops past the deck root close the overlay. * ''Layout templates'' — `mm.slide-layout` selects a wikitext template under `$:/plugins/rimir/present/layouts/`. Ships with `default`, `title`, `two-column`, `quote`, `image`, `full`. Add your own by creating a layout tiddler with the matching name. * ''Presenter notes + help overlays'' — `N` toggles notes (configurable field), `?` opens the keyboard cheat sheet. * ''Activated by state-tiddler'' — wrap `$present` in `$reveal` to gate it on an "is presenting" state; companion plugins wire a Play button that flips the state. !! Owners that don't exist or have no slides are silently skipped. | The mindmap plugin wires this filter to `$present`'s `slides=` via the page-template tiddler `$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/templates/present-overlay`. !! State tiddlers |!Tiddler |!Purpose |!Set by | |`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/present-target` |Title of the presentation tiddler to play |Play buttons (header + modebar ▶), Shift+F2 hotkey | |`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/present-open` |`yes` while overlay is open |Play button + Esc/× close action | |`$:/config/rimir/present/no-esc-close` |`yes` to disable global Esc handler |User config | "},"$:/plugins/rimir/present/doc/tw-internals":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/present/doc/tw-internals","created":"20260513000000000","modified":"20260513000000000","rdt.order":"7","rdt.plugin-key":"present","rdt.plugin-name":"present","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Fullscreen slide player with 2D nav and deep-dive breadcrumb","rdt.section":"TiddlyWiki Internals","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! Why a fixed-position widget instead of `tm-modal`? `tm-modal` produces a centred dialog with a backdrop, intended for forms / confirmations. A slide deck wants the //entire viewport// and its own keyboard semantics — Esc inside a `tm-modal` is hard-coded to close it, which conflicts with the deep-dive stack. A `position: fixed; inset: 0` div sidesteps the framework and gives the widget full control. !! Why is the widget rendered from a `$:/tags/PageTemplate` tiddler? Tagging the host tiddler `$:/tags/PageTemplate` ensures it renders once per page and stays mounted across story-river navigation. The `<$reveal>` wrapper then gates the widget on a state tiddler — the widget exists in the page tree but renders nothing until the state flips to `yes`. That makes "open the deck" a one-line state-tiddler write from anywhere. !! Slide rendering uses `<$tiddler tiddler=…>`, not `<$let currentTiddler=…>` `<$tiddler>` actually re-runs the rendering pipeline with the named tiddler as `currentTiddler` //for the purposes of field references like `{{!!caption}}`//. `<$let currentTiddler="…">` rebinds the variable but doesn't re-base field references. Layouts read fields, so `<$tiddler>` is the right wrapper. !! Link interception caveat Anchors generated by `<$link>` carry the `data-tiddler-title` attribute, which we use for click interception. Anchors from `<$transclude>`-rendered markdown or plain HTML `` won't have it — we fall back to the `href` attribute (stripping a leading `#` if present). External links (whose href doesn't resolve to a tiddler) are left for the browser to handle. !! Layout re-render Each navigation tears down the previous slide widget tree (`removeChildDomNodes` on the layout-transclude subtree) and builds a fresh one. This avoids stale state from heavy embedded widgets (e.g. a mindmap inside a slide). The cost is small for ordinary wikitext slides; if you embed a graph or a long-running plugin, factor in the re-init cost. !! refresh() short-circuit When attributes change, the widget falls back to `refreshSelf()`. When tiddlers change but attrs don't, we re-evaluate the slides filter and compare grid signatures — if equal, fall through to `refreshChildren`. This keeps the overlay stable when the user edits an unrelated tiddler outside the deck. Designed as a generic presentation surface — the slide source is parameterized via a filter — with reveal.js-style 2D navigation, link-driven deep-dive (with a breadcrumb that pops you back), and a pluggable layout system. !! Key features * ''Filter-parameterized'' — pass any filter that yields slide-tiddler titles in order. No coupling to a particular content model. * ''2D navigation'' — `←/→` walk between //sections// (one section per group of slides), `↑/↓` walk between slides //within// the current section. Sections are derived from a configurable group-field on each slide tiddler. * ''Deep-dive via clicks'' — clicking a wikitext link inside a slide pushes the current location onto a navigation stack and renders the linked tiddler as an ad-hoc slide. The breadcrumb at the top shows where you came from; click any segment to pop back. * ''Layout system'' — `mm.slide-layout` (configurable field) maps to a layout template under `$:/plugins/rimir/present/layouts/`. Ships with `default`, `title`, `two-column`, `quote`, `image`, `full`. Author your own by adding tiddlers with the matching name. * ''Notes & help overlays'' — `N` toggles presenter notes (read from a configurable field). `?` opens the keyboard cheat sheet. * ''Engine-agnostic'' — does not depend on a mindmap, list, or any specific producer. Companion plugins (e.g. `rimir/mindmap` v0.3+) supply the filter; this plugin just plays. !! Prerequisites * TiddlyWiki 5.3.0+ * Optional: `rimir/theme` for the shared `rr-` style hooks * Optional: `rimir/doc-template` for the branded documentation tab !! Quick start Render the player anywhere with a filter that yields slide-tiddler titles: ``` <$present slides="[tag[Slides]sort[mm.slide-order]]" section-field="mm.slide-of" layout-field="mm.slide-layout" caption-field="caption" notes-field="mm.slide-notes" title="My deck" /> ``` Wrap with `$reveal` if you want to gate the overlay on a state tiddler: ``` <$reveal state="$:/state/rimir/present/open" text="yes" type="match"> <$present slides={{{ [mm-presentation-slides[]] }}} title=<> /> ``` See the //documentation// tab for layouts, keyboard reference, and the mindmap integration.
